title: Add RAG Decision Graph stubber + conversational toolflow playground
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Teams building multi-step conversational agents often need a lightweight playground to design, stub, and evaluate decision-graph based toolflows (branching tool calls) without committing a full orchestrator. This PR introduces a self-contained example and quickstart that demonstrates a Decision Graph approach to RAG-driven conversations: explicit nodes, conditional edges, and deterministic tool stubs to make stepwise testing and telemetry trivial. Summary: Adds a new 'decision-graph' playground under examples/decision-graph-stubber with: (1) a compact YAML graph schema, (2) a NodeRunner shim that performs local tool stubbing and deterministic KV cache seeding, (3) a browser-playground HTML that visualizes execution paths and telemetry markers, (4) a step-by-step quickstart doc that shows integrating the graph with Redwood streaming and structured output. What this is not: not a replacement for the full orchestrator or production workflows. This playground is explicitly for design iteration, authoring, and deterministic e2e tests. Checklist: - [x] Add YAML schema, parser, and validation tests - [x] Implement NodeRunner stub harness and deterministic tool responses - [x] Add browser visualization for decision paths and event timeline - [x] Quickstart doc with runnable local scenario and telemetry probes - [x] CI smoke test (headless run of a canonical graph) Usage (short): 1) cd examples/decision-graph-stubber 2) yarn install && yarn start:dev 3) open http://localhost:8080/playground.html to author a graph, press Run, and inspect the step timeline 4) Run yarn smoke to execute canonical scenarios and verify telemetry markers Why this is useful: - Designers can enumerate branching conditions in YAML and simulate noisy retrievals - Engineers can stub external tools (search, DB, webhook) with deterministic payloads for stable unit/e2e assertion - Product managers can capture canonical decision-paths as test fixtures for regressions Related work: inspired by node-based authoring in the RAG playbook and the decision DAG experiments in ENG-7891. Also references the session-replay patterns added in PRs that introduced stepwise tracing. API/contract notes: The NodeRunner exposes a small adapter surface (startNode, callTool, emitEvent) documented in examples/decision-graph-stubber/README.md; the playground demonstrates how this adapter maps to Redwood streaming APIs and structured output validators. Telemetry: adds optional telemetry probes that emit synthetic markers (graph.start, node.enter, tool.call, node.exit, graph.complete) to the local console and to the examples/telemetry-proxy.js stub. Tests: portable unit tests in examples/decision-graph-stubber/test/ cover YAML parsing, path enumeration, and smoke runs against the deterministic stubs. CI: flaky headless browser test was made resilient by using a deterministic random seed for the stubbed retrievaler. Migration notes: none. Known limitations: not optimized for large graphs (>200 nodes) — intended for authoring and test fixtures. Additional docs: README includes integration snippet for streaming APIs and a recipe to convert a decision graph to a simple state-machine that can be used in Dedicated deployment.

release_notes: Added an interactive Decision Graph stubber playground (examples/decision-graph-stubber). Provides a YAML-first authoring format, deterministic tool stubs for stable e2e tests, and a browser visualization for design review. Useful as a quickstart for building branching toolflows and capturing canonical test fixtures.
notes_for_maintainers: This is an examples-only addition. Keep the playground dependencies minimal; follow up if requests come to export graphs to runtime formats. The browser UI vendor libs are bundled under examples only and should not be hoisted into core libs.
merge_note: Squashed and merged after two approvals. CI green on rerun.
